## SWE.3 TEMPLATE PER SOFTWARE UNIT
====================================

### Software Unit: Command Parser

1. Responsibilities  
   - Handles UART byte parsing and validation to determine flap position command (SWE-REQ-001, 002, 003, 015, 022).
   - Does not handle scheduling, error code propagation, or hardware register specifics.

2. Internal Data Design  
   - Static structure for command byte (latest only; no queue).
   - Flags: valid/invalid state.
   - Config: allowed position map (table).

3. State Machine  
   - States: {INIT, WAIT_RX, VALID, INVALID}. Events: UART RX event, data parse, data not supported.
   - Transitions: INIT→WAIT_RX→(VALID/INVALID), INVALID→WAIT_RX (on flush).
   - Actions: On VALID: pass command to Flap Control Logic. On INVALID: clear, no action.

4. Algorithms & Control Flow  
   - On UART RX: check byte against allowed table; set valid/invalid, store if new.
   - On duplicate/invalid: ignore.

5. Interfaces (APIs)  
   - Provided: get_latest_command() → position, valid-flag
   - Required: UART_get_byte() (abstracted by device interface)
   - Error: invalid command is reported via valid-flag only (no error code)

6. Error Handling 
   - Unsupported/invalid commands ignored. On buffer overflow: latest overwrites (SWE-REQ-003).

7. Resource & Timing Considerations  
   - Invocation: only on UART RX event
   - WCET: <<1ms (parsing/validation, table lookup)
   - Not re-entrant (latest byte only, static state)

8. Traceability  
   - SWE-REQ-001, SWE-REQ-002, SWE-REQ-003, SWE-REQ-015, SWE-REQ-022

---

### Software Unit: Flap Control Logic

1. Responsibilities  
   - Decides when to move actuator flap, manages current/target state.
   - Handles state/movement only; no scheduling or direct HW interaction.

2. Internal Data Design  
   - Static state: current position, last commanded position, in-motion flag.
   - Config: movement limits as static constants/table.

3. State Machine  
   - States: {IDLE, MOVING, TARGET_REACHED, FAULT}.
   - Events: New command, feedback, error.
   - Transitions: IDLE→MOVING (on delta det.), MOVING→TARGET_REACHED (on feedback match), →FAULT (on error), FAULT→IDLE (on recovery).

4. Algorithms & Control Flow  
   - On valid new command, compare with feedback; initiate move only if different (SWE-REQ-006).
   - Stop move if target reached or error.

5. Interfaces (APIs)  
   - Provided: issue_movement_cmd(target_pos)
   - Required: Feedback Processor (current position), Motor Driver (invoke action), LED Handler (state update)
   - Error: Issues safe-idle request on error.

6. Error Handling  
   - Fault detected via invalid feedback or move error: enter FAULT, stop motor/notify LED.

7. Resource & Timing Considerations  
   - Called on command/feedback event.
   - WCET: <1ms (compare, logical checks)
   - Not re-entrant.

8. Traceability  
   - SWE-REQ-004, SWE-REQ-005, SWE-REQ-006, SWE-REQ-023, SWE-REQ-024, SWE-REQ-031

---

### Software Unit: Motor Driver

1. Responsibilities  
   - Drives DC motor via logical GPIO/PWM as commanded. Enforces STOP/safe mode.

2. Internal Data Design  
   - Static: direction, enable, PWM duty (no dynamic alloc).
   - Config: motor limits as constants.

3. State Machine  
   - State: NONE – pure command->output logic; no internal transition beyond on/off.

4. Algorithms & Control Flow  
   - On command: set outputs as given; on stop/error: all outputs off.

5. Interfaces (APIs)  
   - Provided: drive_motor(dir, enable), stop_motor(), get_status()
   - Required: Called by Flap Control.

6. Error Handling  
   - On error: cease all output (see safe state); report via get_status().

7. Resource & Timing Considerations  
   - WCET: <<1ms per call.
   - Not re-entrant (single request at a time).

8. Traceability  
   - SWE-REQ-007, SWE-REQ-008, SWE-REQ-016, SWE-REQ-025, SWE-REQ-036, SWE-REQ-038

---

### Software Unit: Feedback Processor

1. Responsibilities  
   - Acquires/validates ADC, interprets to logical position. No self-learning.

2. Internal Data Design  
   - Static: latest ADC sample, mapped position, validity flag.
   - Config: position map (lookup table), boundary constants.

3. State Machine  
   - States: {INIT, READY, INVALID}
   - Events: ADC sample, mapping calc, out-of-range or valid.
   - Transitions: INIT→READY (first valid), INVALID↔READY (on error recovery/correct).

4. Algorithms & Control Flow  
   - On ADC sample: bound check, table lookup, set position/validity.
   - If out-of-bounds: INVALID state.

5. Interfaces (APIs)  
   - Provided: get_position() → (pos, valid), update()
   - Required: ADC device API (abstracted)

6. Error Handling  
   - Bad/missing ADC: report INVALID, refuse update to Flap Logic.

7. Resource & Timing Considerations  
   - WCET: <1ms/sample
   - Not re-entrant (uses static last sample)

8. Traceability  
   - SWE-REQ-010, SWE-REQ-011, SWE-REQ-017, SWE-REQ-027, SWE-REQ-028, SWE-REQ-030

---

### Software Unit: LED Status Handler

1. Responsibilities  
   - Controls status LEDs, enforces one-hot position, only event-driven changes.

2. Internal Data Design  
   - Static: current state (LED bits).
   - Config: mapping table pos↔LED.

3. State Machine  
   - State: NONE – pure output mirror; state set only on valid event.

4. Algorithms & Control Flow  
   - On new event: update LED based on position or error state; only one green at a time.

5. Interfaces (APIs)  
   - Provided: set_led_state(pos), indicate_error(), set_power_led()
   - Required: Event/call from Flap Control

6. Error Handling  
   - On error: indicate_error(), do not change otherwise.

7. Resource & Timing Considerations  
   - Fast logic, <<1ms/call
   - Not re-entrant

8. Traceability  
   - SWE-REQ-012, SWE-REQ-013, SWE-REQ-014, SWE-REQ-018, SWE-REQ-021, SWE-REQ-039

---

### Software Unit: System Startup/Initialization

1. Responsibilities  
   - One-time init for all data/hardware abstraction, triggers safe states.

2. Internal Data Design  
   - Static init status, local config data.

3. State Machine  
   - State: NONE (single pass only)

4. Algorithms & Control Flow  
   - On entry: initialize all units, output safe states, check feedback, set LEDs.

5. Interfaces (APIs)  
   - Provided: system_init()
   - Required: Calls all other units’ init/config routines

6. Error Handling  
   - Any unit error: flag, halt, indicate via LEDs

7. Resource & Timing Considerations  
   - Only on boot, <<10ms total
   - Not re-entrant

8. Traceability  
   - SWE-REQ-020

---
